Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Abhinav Singh Hon'ble Vivek Varma,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicants and Sri Nagendra Kumar Mishra, learned Brief Holder for the State- opposite party no. 1.
2.

The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed with the prayer to quash the entire proceedings of Criminal Case No. 13427 of 2020, State v. Braj Kishore and others, arising out of Case Crime No.
328 of 2020, under Sections 498A, 323 I.P.C. and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Khatauli, District Muzaffarnagar pending in the Court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Muzaffarnagar as well as charge-sheet dated 11.10.2020 and the cognizance order dated 03.12.2020 passed in the said case, on the basis of compromise between the parties.
3.

sentences.text: As per the report of the Mediation Centre dated 04.03.2023, the parties have amicably settled their dispute and further agreed to withdraw the cases going on between them.
The relevant portion of the report is extracted hereinbelow:
"6. The parties hereto confirm and declare that they have voluntarily and of their own free will arrived at this Settlement Agreement in the presence of the Mediator/Conciliator.

7. The following settlement has been arrived at between the Parties hereto:-
a) That the parties stated that they are living together as husband and wife forgetting all previous disputes and differences and stated that they are fully satisfied with this reunion and further they want to continue it for the rest of their lives.
b) That the parties undertake not to commit any kind of cruelty against each other in any manner whatsoever.
c) That it has been agreed between the parties that they will behave properly living in peaceful and cordial atmosphere.
d) That the husband undertakes to take care of his wife and fulfill all essential requirements and amenities to her in future.

e) That it has also been agreed between the parties that all the cases filed by them against each other or their family members regarding present matrimonial dispute Manish Sharma And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98462021/
2 shall be withdrawn by the parties concerned by taking appropriate steps before the Court/ authority concerned.

entities.text: Manish Sharma And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: f) That the parties will not file any fresh case against each other in respect of this matrimonial dispute.
They have no claim against each other in future also.
(g) That it has been agreed between the parties that they shall not violate the terms and conditions of this settlement otherwise the aggrieved party will be free to take legal recourse.

8.- By signing this Agreement the Parties hereto state that the Application U/s 482 No. 8671 of 2022 and all disputes and differences in this regard have been amicably settled by the Parties hereto through the process of Conciliation/Mediation."
5. The opposite party no. 2- informant and the victim (wife) had also appeared before the Mediation Centre and were duly identified by their counsel.
They have not filed any affidavit in the present case disputing the aforesaid facts.

6. In view of the fact that the dispute appears to be purely of a personal nature being a matrimonial dispute that has been mutually settled between the parties, to their satisfaction, no useful purpose would be served in allowing such a prosecution to proceed any further.

7. Thus, in view of the well settled principles of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in B.S.
Joshi v. State of Haryana, 2003(4) SCC 675, as well as Nikhil Merchant v. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, J.T., 2008 (9) SC 192, the proceedings of the aforesaid case are hereby set aside.

sentences.text: 8. Learned counsel for the applicants further submits that as per the terms of the earlier order dated 14.07.2022 passed by this Court, the amount to be paid to the wife (victim), as expenses, has not been paid till date.
In such circumstances, liberty is granted to the applicants to move an appropriate application before the Mediation and Conciliation Centre of this Court within a period of four weeks from today.
9. The present application is, accordingly, allowed.
